    <!-- GROWING IN ARIZONA -->
    <section class="gy-section">

      <div class="gy-growing-layout">

        <div class="gy-growing-copy">

          <div class="gy-section-heading">

            <span class="gy-section-label">
              Growing in Arizona
            </span>

            <h2>
              Growing Food in the Low Desert
            </h2>

          </div>

          <p>
            Arizona includes very different growing environments, from the hot
            low desert to much cooler high-elevation regions. The Green Yard’s
            current Arizona tours are concentrated in the Phoenix metropolitan
            area, where growers are working with intense summer heat, limited
            rainfall, mild winters, and occasional freezes.
          </p>

          <p>
            The landscapes featured here show how individual growers respond to
            those conditions in different ways. Shade, irrigation, mulch,
            canopy, plant placement, and microclimates all appear throughout
            the tours, but each grower brings their own experience and approach
            to creating a productive landscape in the desert.
          </p>

          <p>
            Rather than presenting one formula for growing in Arizona, these tours
            are an opportunity to learn directly from the people doing the
            work: what they grow, what has succeeded, what has struggled, and
            how their landscapes continue to change through experience.
          </p>

        </div>


        <aside class="gy-growing-note">

          <strong>
            About These Arizona Tours
          </strong>

          <p>
            The Green Yard’s Arizona tours currently focus on the Phoenix metro
            and surrounding low desert. As the tour library grows, this page
            can expand to include growers and food-producing landscapes from
            other parts of Arizona as well.
          </p>

        </aside>

      </div>

    </section>


    <!-- CLIMATE SNAPSHOT -->
    <section class="gy-section">

      <div class="gy-section-heading">

        <span class="gy-section-label">
          Climate Snapshot
        </span>

        <h2>
          Arizona Low-Desert Growing Context
        </h2>

        <p>
          These broad points provide context for the Phoenix-area low desert where
          The Green Yard’s current Arizona tours are located. The individual
          tours show how growers actually respond to these conditions on the ground.
        </p>

      </div>


      <div class="gy-climate-grid">

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Climate</span>
          <strong>Hot Desert</strong>
          <p>
            Mediterranean, coastal, desert, mountain, and inland climates all
            occur within the state.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Growing Season</span>
          <strong>Nearly Year-Round</strong>
          <p>
            Different crops thrive at different times of year, allowing growers to
            keep something productive through much of the calendar.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Summer</span>
          <strong>Extreme Heat</strong>
          <p>
            Phoenix summers regularly bring extreme heat, creating one of the
            biggest challenges for young and heat-sensitive plants.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Winter</span>
          <strong>Mild With Freeze Risk</strong>
          <p>
            Most winter days are mild, but occasional cold nights and freezes can
            challenge tropical and subtropical plants.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Water</span>
          <strong>Limited Rainfall</strong>
          <p>
            Growers depend heavily on irrigation while using mulch, soil-building,
            and other approaches to help conserve moisture.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Common Theme</span>
          <strong>Microclimates</strong>
          <p>
            The tours repeatedly show growers using shade, canopy, structures, and
            plant placement to create different conditions within one property.
          </p>
        </div>

      </div>

    </section>
